output.scope_note: The paper reports room-temperature ionic conductivities of Li-salt-containing PEO-PVC solid polymer electrolytes, which are solid Li-ion conductors, so it is in scope.

records.evidence_quote: The highest ionic conductivity was 2.3×10-5 S cm-1 for erbium oxide nanofiller and almost five order greater than pure polymer blend
records.notes: Er2O3 is a 10 wt.% nanofiller in the (PEO-PVC)+LiPF6 blend (sample PPLE). Impedance was measured at room temperature per the Experimental section. The abstract gives the same value as ~2.3×10-5 S cm-1. Filler is not a dopant, so dopants is empty.

records.material_as_written: PP (pure PEO-PVC polymer blend, no salt)
records.evidence_quote: The ionic conductivity of pure polymer blend was 6.4×10-10 S cm-1.
records.notes: Pure blend without LiPF6 salt, so it is not a Li-conducting material in a meaningful sense; included because the paper reports its conductivity. Temperature is given only as room temperature in the EIS section, so it is not converted.

records.evidence_quote: is in good agreement with value obtained using the bulk resistance (R b) from impedance plot given as; 6.40×10-10 S cm-1 and 7.10×10-7 S cm-1 respectively.
records.notes: Value is from the bulk resistance of the impedance plot, matched to the polymer salt (PPL) sample by the word 'respectively'. The JPL fit gives 4.66×10-7 S cm-1 for this sample, which is not recorded. Temperature is room temperature per the EIS section.
